At WWDC 2021, Apple announced support for storing driver's licenses in Apple Wallet on iPhone. At the time, Apple marketed it as the final step to "completely free yourself from a physical wallet."

Here are the states that will support the Apple Wallet driver's license feature next…

Apple Wallet ID Support

In the five years since Apple announced this feature, support has gradually expanded across the United States. Currently, iPhone and Apple Watch users in 14 states and Puerto Rico can add a driver's license or state ID to Apple Wallet. You can see the full list here:

Where is this feature coming next? Here's what we know so far.

The following seven states have confirmed they are working on Apple Wallet driver's license support, have been listed by Apple as partners, and/or have appeared in Apple's code:

  • Kentucky (launching "summer" 2026)
  • North Carolina (launching early 2027)
  • Oklahoma (in progress, launch date unknown)
  • Utah (in progress, launch date unknown)
  • Virginia (in progress, launch date unknown)
  • Connecticut (status unclear, previously listed by Apple as a partner)
  • Mississippi (status unclear, previously listed by Apple as a partner)

Meanwhile, the Secure Technology Alliance has been tracking the rollout of mobile driver's license support across the US. The following states have begun exploring mobile ID support through legislation or studies, but have not been mentioned by Apple:

  • Indiana
  • Vermont
  • New Jersey
  • Florida
  • South Carolina
  • Tennessee
  • Missouri
  • Nevada
  • Wyoming

It's worth noting that progress can vary greatly from state to state. A state exploring or developing digital ID support does not necessarily mean it will eventually launch, nor that it will come to Apple Wallet.

Summary

As you can see, the rollout of Apple Wallet driver's license support across the United States remains quite scattered.

However, you don't have to wait for your state to support the Apple Wallet digital ID feature to try it out.

Apple launched a new Digital ID feature last year, powered by your US passport. Although it's not your driver's license, it allows you to use your iPhone at TSA security checkpoints in over 250 airports across the country.

Have you stored your ID or driver's license in Apple Wallet on your iPhone? Have you actually used it? Share with us in the comments.
